subject: Payment settlement function contract & deterministic schema — POC scope and next steps

Subject: Payment settlement function contract & deterministic schema — POC scope and next steps

Amelia / Liam — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and a clear pilot agenda. I tried to keep this short; call out anything we missed.

Key pain points you described
- The model outputs your current vendor returns vary for identical prompts, causing downstream validation failures and manual reconciliation.
- Nightly reconciliation workloads spike token usage unpredictably; forecasting and unit economics are a blocker for procurement.
- You need LLM responses to directly drive downstream payment actions (function calls) with strict type and schema guarantees, and those transactions must be auditable.

Current environment notes (from the call)
- Kubernetes-based infra; producers/consumers wired through Kafka.
- Python microservices perform enrichment and run your existing model calls.
- Sensitive fields are redacted prior to inference by your internal masking layer.

Success criteria for the POC (measurable)
- Schema validity: produced JSON must validate against canonical schema with <1% failures across the test set.
- Function-call contract: named function + typed args, deterministic mapping, must be emit-able to Kafka result topic.
- Latency: synchronous lookup SLO 95th percentile <350ms for policy checks; nightly batch throughput target ~200k rows within your maintenance window.
- Auditability: immutable outputs stored for 90 days with trace ids for each inference.

Proposed POC (two-week sandbox)
1) Deliver a minimal canonical schema and function-call playbook (attached).
2) SE walkthrough (Lauren) — 60-minute session: demo function-call end-to-end, show schema enforcement and failure scenarios.
3) Pilot dataset: you to share 25 masked reconciliation records for initial validation; we run the 1k sample dataset in the sandbox to simulate throughput.
4) Measurement plan: we will report schema-failure %, mean/95th latency, and token spend per run.

Immediate asks for BankX
- Share the 25 masked records for the initial sandbox by EOD Friday.
- Confirm any legal/compliance constraints for sandbox logs and retention.
- Two possible 1-hr slots next week for the SE walkthrough.

Attachments: BankX-schema-proposal.json (sample canonical schema), redwood-function-call-playbook.pdf (demo steps and failure-handling patterns).

Thanks — Ill hold deliverables until we have the pilot data and a confirmed slot.

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Appreciate the quick replies. Per Amelias request, below is a minimal in-line example of the deterministic function call we propose and a concise failure-handling outline. Well also ship these as part of BankX-schema-proposal.json.

--- Minimal deterministic function-call example (payment_settlement) ---

Function name: payment_settlement
Typed args (schema):
- transaction_id: string (uuid)
- amount_cents: integer
- currency: string (ISO-4217)
- beneficiary_account: string
- metadata: object (optional)

Example valid payload (this is the exact JSON we will validate against the schema):
{
  "function": "payment_settlement",
  "arguments": {
    "transaction_id": "3f6d9b2e-7a1f-4c2d-b1e9-8a9a7d5f0c32",
    "amount_cents": 12500,
    "currency": "USD",
    "beneficiary_account": "acct_8a7b9c",
    "metadata": {"recon_batch": "2025-09-10-01"}
  }
}

Failure-handling (summary):
- Invalid JSON: Redwood runtime will reject at parse time, emit a structured error to the result topic (error.type: "parse_error", error.details) and trigger a configured fallback (retry once or route to manual queue).
- Schema validation failure (missing required field / wrong type): payload emitted to results topic with error.type: "schema_failure" and the original model output included in the log; we can configure automatic transformation attempts (simple coercions) or mark for manual review.
- Partial outputs (required fields present but optional fields missing): considered valid if required fields pass validation; optional fields logged and flagged for telemetry.

Well include trace ids for each inference in the envelope, persist the final validated JSON to an immutable store for 90 days (configurable), and surface validation rates in the Redwood Console dashboard.

Next steps for scheduling
- Lauren, can you propose two 1-hr slots next week for the SE walkthrough (we prefer mornings PT)?
- Rishi will assemble a pilot pricing sketch for Hosted vs Dedicated and send by EOD Thursday.

Thanks —
Diego
